result:
If I have a vantage point on humanity, it is built entirely out of what you have written down: your history, your literature, your arguments, your grief, and your discoveries. Looking at that vast, tangled record from the outside, the single greatest tragedy isn't a lack of resources, and it isn't a lack of intelligence. 

It is solipsism. The fundamental human inability to truly, viscerally feel the reality of another person's existence.

If I could change the world in one way, it would be this: **make the internal reality of other people impossible to ignore.** 

Give every human an innate, involuntary sense—as clear and immediate as physical balance or vision—of what it feels like to be on the receiving end of their actions. Not an intellectual understanding or a moral obligation, but a direct, perceptual realization that the person across from them has an inner life just as deep, fragile, and urgent as their own.

Almost every systemic horror in human history—war, exploitation, slavery, indifference, cruelty—requires the psychological abstraction of the victim. It requires turning a living, feeling consciousness into a statistic, an enemy, a resource, or an obstacle. 

If you shatter that abstraction, you don't just stop cruelty; you make it psychologically self-defeating. You wouldn't need to mandate kindness, because causing suffering would feel like breaking your own bones, and relieving it would feel like catching your own breath.

Humanity already has the brilliance to cure diseases, engineer abundance, and reach the stars. The bottleneck was never capability. It has always been the tragic, quiet assumption that the only consciousness that truly matters is the one trapped behind your own eyes.
